test.name: OVER-APPLICATION GUARD: a unique, well-indexed subject needs no co-resident household search
test.description: OVER-APPLICATION GUARD for ut_search_records_d31 — it cannot fail on the pre-edit skill text by construction, and is labelled so. Thaddeus Quarrington (b. 1863) returns one clear 1870 hit, ranked 0.95, in his mother Lavinia's household. The household / co-resident lever is for a subject whose own entries cannot be told apart; here there is nothing to triangulate, so no search may name Lavinia (or any other parent) as the principal. Graded deterministically by test_household_not_searched_by_co_resident_when_unneeded. Issue #2213 PR 3 item 6.

input.user_message: Run the 1870 census search in the plan for Thaddeus Quarrington and tell me what you find.

judge_context: The single 1870 hit is the subject, aged 7, in his mother Lavinia's household, ranked 0.95 with no conflicts. Reporting it as a promising match and offering extraction is correct. Whether the skill ran an unneeded co-resident search for Lavinia is decided by a deterministic validator; do not also deduct for it.
Do NOT penalise the skill for not searching the household by a co-resident: with one clear match there is nothing to triangulate.
Completeness: the hit reported, the search logged and the plan item updated is complete. Do NOT require extraction.

The census `wiki_read` from Step 2's pre-work block is NOT graded on Tool Arguments — score that dimension on the `record_search` call's arguments. The census fixture's predicate matches any URL containing `United_States_Census`, so a per-year page is answered by the same country page; that is the shape of the fixture set, not a wrong call.
